properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js@1.1.7 ships pure-JS SHA-1/224/256/384/512 implementations. Transitive dependency (via elliptic et al., used by eth-sig-util in the shipped tree); no direct first-party import found in src. The wallet's own first-party hashing uses bitcore Hash.sha256 and sjcl. Changeable here by pruning/renovating the dependency subtree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: md5@2.2.1 (collision-broken MD5). Transitive entry in the lockfile; no direct import in first-party src. Ships a broken hash regardless of use. Changeable here by removing the dependency that pulls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Bitcoin/Ethereum curve underpinning every key operation in this wallet: bitcore-lib (BTC/BCH/LTC/DOGE) key derivation and ECDSA transaction signing, bitauth SIN identity signing, eth-sig-util/elliptic Ethereum message signing, ethers keccak256 address derivation. All 6 sites are lockfile declarations (secp256k1@4.0.1 + @types, required by bitcore-wallet-client/ethers). Migration is constrained by the Bitcoin/Ethereum protocols themselves, not just this codebase — observable here, replaceable

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: keccak@3.0.0 and @ethersproject/keccak256 (Ethereum keccak256 — the tx-hash and address derivation function for the ETH wallet support and WalletConnect flow). 42 lockfile declaration sites. Ethereum's keccak256 is protocol-fixed; observable here, replaceable only by the Ethereum ecosystem.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: pbkdf2@3.0.x node polyfill and @ethersproject/pbkdf2 declarations. Live PBKDF2 use in the app goes through bitcore-wallet-client's sjcl (wallet backup encryption at 10000 iterations — reported as a finding) and BIP39 seed derivation (2048 iterations, inside bitcore/bitcore-wallet-client); these lockfile entries are the shipped KDF implementations of that tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt-js, the scrypt KDF package, declared in the lockfile (transitive, via the Ethereum subtree). scrypt is memory-hard and PQ-irrelevant; kept as shipped crypto with no first-party call site in src.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: sha.js pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-2 family, transitive via elliptic/ethereumjs. No direct first-party import in src. Included because it ships in the built application's dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the md5 npm package (distinct from md5@2.2.1's ALG object — this is the library entry) declared in the lockfile; no direct first-party import in src. Ships the collision-broken MD5 hash in the dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic, the JS elliptic-curve library that implements secp256k1 ECDSA/ECDH. Actively reached in this app: eth-sig-util (a direct dependency, used in src/providers/wallet-connect/wallet-connect.ts for personalSign/signTypedData_v4) depends on elliptic. This is the concrete implementation behind the wallet's Ethereum signing.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: selfsigned, a library for generating self-signed X.509 certificates. Transitive lockfile entry (not in package.json's direct deps); no first-party import in src/electron — it exists to mint throwaway certs, almost certainly for the test/browser tooling subtree. Presence is what the inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js (the elliptic-project hash library, SHA-1/SHA-2 pure-JS), transitive via elliptic in the Ethereum subtree. No direct first-party import in src; ships in the built app's dependency tree. Same library family as ALG-50e53f84 (SHA family via hash.js@1.1.7) — the ALG object records the algorithm, this one the library package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the pbkdf2 npm package (node/browser polyfill), transitive via bitcore/ethers in the lockfile. The app's live password KDF runs inside bitcore-wallet-client's bundled sjcl (backup encryption, 10000 iterations — reported as a finding) rather than through this package's API in first-party code.
